summary: Fever is a temporary increase in body temperature, often due to an illness or infection. Normal body temperature is around 98.6°F (37°C).
home_care: Drink plenty of fluids like water, ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts), coconut water, and herbal tea.
Rest adequately in a cool, ventilated room.
Apply lukewarm water sponge compresses to the forehead and armpits.
Take light, easily digestible meals (khichdi, soups).
red_flags: Fever exceeding 103°F (39.4°C) or persisting for more than 3 consecutive days.
Fever accompanied by stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, or breathing difficulty.
Presence of unusual skin rash or petechiae.
source: WHO Clinical Guidelines & ICMR Fever Protocol

condition: Chest Pain and Cardiac Distress (Seene mein Dard)
summary: Acute chest pain, pressure, or squeezing sensation radiating to the left arm, neck, or jaw can be a life-threatening cardiac event.
symptoms: Radiation of pain to left arm, neck, back, or jaw
home_care: DO NOT WAIT. Call emergency services (112 or 108 in India) immediately.
Have the person sit down in a comfortable position and stay calm.
Loosen any tight clothing around the neck and waist.
If prescribed by a cardiologist and not allergic, chew an Aspirin (300mg) while awaiting ambulance.
red_flags: ANY severe sudden crushing chest pain with breathing difficulty is a MEDICAL EMERGENCY.
source: American Heart Association (AHA) & AIIMS Emergency Medicine Guidelines

condition: Common Cold, Cough, and Sore Throat (Khansi / Zukaam)
summary: Viral infection of the upper respiratory tract causing runny nose, congestion, mild cough, and throat irritation.
home_care: Steam inhalation 2-3 times daily with warm water.
Warm saline water gargling (half tsp salt in warm water) 3 times a day.
Honey with ginger or warm turmeric milk for soothing throat irritation.
Maintain adequate hydration with warm soups and liquids.
red_flags: Cough lasting longer than 2-3 weeks.
Coughing up blood (hemoptysis) or thick rust-colored phlegm.
Severe wheezing or difficulty catching breath.
source: CDC Respiratory Infection Guidelines & MoHFW India

condition: Acute Acidity, Gastritis, and GERD (Pet mein Jalan / Acidity)
summary: Excess stomach acid production causing burning sensation in the chest (heartburn), bloating, and sour belching.
symptoms: Burning sensation in upper abdomen and chest
Nausea after spicy or oily meals
home_care: Drink cold milk or coconut water for immediate acid neutralization.
Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large heavy dinners.
Avoid lying down immediately after eating (keep a 2-3 hour gap).
Avoid spicy, oily, deep-fried foods, caffeine, and carbonated beverages.
red_flags: Severe vomiting with blood or black tarry stools (melena).
Difficulty or pain while swallowing food.
Unexplained sudden weight loss with severe persistent pain.
source: Indian Journal of Gastroenterology & NHS Clinical Protocol

summary: Head pain ranging from tension headaches due to stress/dehydration to throbbing unilateral migraines with light sensitivity.
symptoms: Dull aching tension or pulsating one-sided pain
Sensitivity to bright light and loud sounds (photophobia/phonophobia)
home_care: Rest in a quiet, dark room with eyes closed.
Apply a cold or warm pack to the forehead or back of the neck.
Drink 2-3 glasses of water to rule out dehydration.
Practice gentle neck stretching and deep breathing exercises.
red_flags: Sudden, severe 'thunderclap' headache (worst headache of your life).
Headache following a head injury or trauma.
Headache with blurred vision, speech slurring, or weakness in arms/legs (Stroke signs).
source: International Headache Society & ICMR Neurology Guidelines

summary: Mosquito-borne viral infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, characterized by high fever, severe retro-orbital pain, and joint aches.
symptoms: Severe joint and muscle pain ('break-bone fever')
Skin rash appearing 2-5 days after fever
home_care: Complete bed rest and aggressive fluid intake (ORS, papaya leaf juice extract, coconut water, fresh fruit juices).
Take only Paracetamol for fever; AVOID Aspirin, Ibuprofen, and NSAIDs as they increase bleeding risks.
Regular monitoring of Complete Blood Count (CBC) and platelet count.
red_flags: Bleeding from gums, nose, or blood in vomit/stools.
Severe continuous abdominal pain or persistent vomiting.
Sudden drop in platelet count below 50,000 / μL.
source: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) & WHO

condition: Type 2 Diabetes and Blood Sugar Management (Madhumeh / Sugar)
summary: Metabolic disorder characterized by elevated blood glucose levels due to insulin resistance or insufficient insulin production.
home_care: Follow a low-glycemic, high-fiber diet rich in green vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins.
Engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise daily (brisk walking).
Regularly monitor fasting and post-prandial blood sugar levels.
Never skip prescribed anti-diabetic medications or insulin doses.
red_flags: Blood sugar reading above 350 mg/dL or below 60 mg/dL (Hypoglycemia).
Fruity breath odor, confusion, rapid deep breathing (Diabetic Ketoacidosis).
Non-healing foot ulcers with numbness or discoloration.
source: Research Society for the Study of Diabetes in India (RSSDI) & ADA

condition: Acute Diarrhea, Vomiting, and Dehydration (Dast / Ulti)
summary: Frequent loose watery stools and nausea usually caused by viral, bacterial, or foodborne gastrointestinal infections.
symptoms: Dry mouth, sunken eyes, and dark urine
home_care: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) is the single most critical treatment — sip small amounts continuously.
Consume the BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast / Curd rice.
Zinc supplementation for 14 days under medical advice.
Avoid milk products, sugary drinks, fried foods, and caffeine.
red_flags: Inability to keep any liquids down for over 12 hours.
Presence of blood or mucus in stools (Dysentery).
Extreme lethargy, no urination for >8 hours, or fainting spells.
source: WHO Diarrhoeal Disease Factsheet & UNICEF/ICMR Protocol
